title: Asked AI a tax question? Check it in 3 steps
label: Tax myth vs fact

link.label: AI in accounting and tax 2026 guide (MFA)

hook.sub: Check this before you trust it.

lines: Nina asked a chatbot about her home office.
It was using an old year's rule.

items.t: Ask which tax year it means
Check the math with your records

cta.sub: We'll DM you our AI and tax guide.

captions.instagram:
Chatbots answer tax questions fast and sound sure of themselves. Tax rules change every year, so check before you act.

✔️ The IRS says taxpayers are ultimately responsible for everything on their return, whoever prepares it.
✔️ Its 2026 Dirty Dozen list says not to rely on AI for complex tax questions and to verify any numbers it gives you.
✔️ Three checks: ask which tax year the answer is for, find the rule on irs.gov, and check the math against your own records.

Our AI and tax guide covers where it helps and where to slow down.

captions.pinterest_title: Using AI for Tax Questions? 3 Checks Before You Trust the Answer
captions.pinterest_description: Using ChatGPT or other AI for tax questions: the IRS says you're responsible for your return no matter who prepares it, and to verify any calculations AI gives you. Three checks: confirm the tax year, find the rule on irs.gov, and compare the math with your own records.

sources.fact: 'Taxpayers are ultimately responsible for all the information on their income tax return' regardless of who prepares it (IRS Tax Tip 2023-19); read 2026-10-30
IR-2026-30 (Mar. 5, 2026) Dirty Dozen: taxpayers should not rely on AI-generated responses to complex tax questions and should verify any calculations or information provided by AI; read 2026-10-30
